hook: The thought spiral isn't your anxiety. It's your anxiety looking for a reason.
topic: Why anxious thoughts are symptoms, not causes
body:
**The thought spiral isn't your anxiety. It's your anxiety looking for a reason.**

When your nervous system is activated — when the signal has already fired — your brain does something very specific. It goes looking for a problem that would justify the alarm.

It searches recent memory, upcoming events, unresolved conversations, anything that could explain why the body is responding the way it is.

And it finds something. It always finds something. Not because that thing is the actual cause, but because your brain needs the signal to make sense.

So you end up thinking about that conversation, or that deadline, or that thing you said three months ago — and it feels like those thoughts are causing the anxiety. They aren't. The activation came first. The content of the spiral is the story your brain attached to an already-running signal.

This is why solving the thoughts doesn't solve the anxiety. You can reach a logical resolution on every item in the spiral and still feel just as activated, because you haven't addressed the signal underneath.

Stop trying to think your way out. Address the signal first. The thoughts usually follow.

The protocol for this is in the free guide — link in my bio.
